vectors.description: minimal FETCH with no parameters. Draft-20 deleted the Fetch Type field, the Standalone Fetch and Joining Fetch structures and the inline Start/End Location: Track Namespace and Track Name are now inline fields of FETCH itself and the range travels in the LOCATION_FILTER parameter. A FETCH with no LOCATION_FILTER covers {0,0} through Largest Object inclusive. The codepoint 0x16 did not change, so a draft-19 decoder reads the Number of Track Namespace Fields count as a Fetch Type and mis-parses in silence
FETCH with multi-element namespace

FETCH with a type 0x01 (Relative Start) LOCATION_FILTER, StartGroup=0: the relative form, starting at the Next Group. Section 9.20.9: "If Location Filter Type is 0x01, a relative StartGroup follows." and "StartGroup=0 will start at the Next Group". "When they are omitted from a Fetch, the EndGroup and EndObject are Largest Object." Draft-22 puts no restriction on which types a FETCH may carry, so this decodes. Draft-20 and draft-21 had no type and inferred the shape from the parameter's byte Length; draft-22 leads with a Location Filter Type instead: "The Location Filter Type dictates which optional variable-length integer fields follow, and how they are interpreted." Its numbers are not draft-19's either, whose 0x1 was Next Group Start. With every field below 128 these bytes are identical to draft-21's, where the byte after 0x21 was a Length that happened to equal the field count, so this vector cannot tell a draft-21 decoder from a draft-22 one; with-filter-next-object and with-filter-noncanonical-field-count are the vectors that can

FETCH with a type 0x01 (Relative Start) LOCATION_FILTER, StartGroup=3, starting 2 groups before the current group. Section 9.20.9: "When they are omitted from a Fetch, the EndGroup and EndObject are Largest Object."

FETCH with a type 0x05 LOCATION_FILTER, the Next Object. Section 9.20.9: "If Location Filter Type is 0x05, no fields follow and it specifies the Next Object." Draft-21 wrote this as a two-field filter with StartGroup and StartObject both 0 (21 02 00 00); draft-22 deleted that special case, so those bytes are now the absolute start {0,0} and the Next Object is these two bytes, with a message Length 2 lower than draft-21's. Draft-22 puts no restriction on which types a FETCH may carry, so this decodes
FETCH with a type 0x02 (Absolute Start) LOCATION_FILTER: absolute start {10,3}, end resolved to Largest Object. Section 9.20.9: "If Location Filter Type is 0x02, StartGroup and StartObject follow."

FETCH with a type 0x03 (Absolute Start, Group End) LOCATION_FILTER: start {10,3}, EndGroupDelta 5 so the End Group is 15, EndObject omitted so all objects in group 15 are included. EndGroupDelta is delta encoded from StartGroup but both groups are absolute, not relative to Largest Object. Section 9.20.9: "If Location Filter Type is 0x03, StartGroup, StartObject, and EndGroupDelta follow."

FETCH with a type 0x04 (Absolute Range) LOCATION_FILTER: the inclusive range {10,3} through {15,7}. Draft-19 encoded a fetch end as the last Object plus 1, with an Object of 0 meaning the whole group; draft-20 dropped both conventions, so a ported encoder that keeps its +1 fetches one object too many

non-canonical FETCH — a type 0x02 LOCATION_FILTER whose StartGroup (10) is encoded as a 2-byte varint (800a) and StartObject (3) as one byte. Section 8.1: "Variable-length integers do not need to be encoded using the minimum number of bytes; any encoding length that can represent the value is valid." The byte after 0x21 is the type, 02, and not the 03 a draft-21 Length would carry: draft-21's 21 03 800a 03, read as draft-22, is a type 0x03 filter missing its EndGroupDelta. This is one of the vectors that separates a draft-22 decoder from a draft-21 one. Decode-only, because a sender always emits the minimal form
FETCH with SUBSCRIBER_PRIORITY parameter (16). Omitted, the publisher uses 128
FETCH with GROUP_ORDER parameter (descending=2). Omitted from a FETCH, the receiver uses Ascending
FETCH with FILL_TIMEOUT parameter (5000ms): the total budget a relay spends waiting for upstream sources before reporting the remainder as Timed-Out gaps

FETCH with FILL_TIMEOUT=0 — the subscriber wants only immediately available Objects and the relay MUST report everything else with the End of Timed-Out Range marker (0x20C). Draft-19 classified these as Unknown gaps
FETCH with INCLUDE_PROPERTIES (0x35) set to 0 — the FETCH_OK should carry an empty Track Properties field
FETCH with AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN parameter (USE_VALUE type=0, value='fetch-token')
FETCH with OBJECTID_FILTER (0x26): SetID 0, Object ID range 2-5
FETCH with PRIORITY_FILTER (0x27): SetID 0, Publisher Priority range 0-63
FETCH with SUBSCRIBER_PRIORITY (16), a type 0x04 LOCATION_FILTER covering {4,0} through {6,9} inclusive, and GROUP_ORDER (ascending=1); demonstrates type-delta ordering across 0x20, 0x21 and 0x22

FETCH whose LOCATION_FILTER carries Location Filter Type 0x40. Section 9.20.9 defines 0x00 through 0x05 and closes the rest: "Any other Location Filter Type is a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION." The type is what says how many fields follow, so a decoder has no way to step over one it does not know. Draft-21 read the same byte as a Length of 64, which runs past the message
vectors.error_detail: Location Filter Type 0x40 is not defined; draft-22 defines 0x00 through 0x05

vectors.description: FETCH whose LOCATION_FILTER is type 0x04 but whose message ends after StartGroup and StartObject. Section 9.20.9: "If Location Filter Type is 0x04, StartGroup, StartObject, EndGroupDelta, and EndObject follow." The control message Length is right and covers every byte here, so the frame is complete and what is malformed is the parameter. The draft does not name the error, and this corpus records PROTOCOL_VIOLATION
vectors.error_detail: a type 0x04 LOCATION_FILTER carries four fields and the message payload ends after two

vectors.description: FETCH whose type 0x03 LOCATION_FILTER has StartGroup = 2^64 - 1 and EndGroupDelta = 1. Section 9.20.9: "If StartGroup + EndGroupDelta exceeds 2^64 - 1, the endpoint MUST close the session with a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION."

FETCH whose type 0x04 LOCATION_FILTER has StartGroup = 2^64 - 1, EndGroupDelta = 1 and EndObject = 0. The overflow rule is not specific to one type; it covers both types that carry an EndGroupDelta, 0x03 and 0x04. Section 9.20.9: "If StartGroup + EndGroupDelta exceeds 2^64 - 1, the endpoint MUST close the session with a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION."

FETCH carrying FILL_PARAMETERS (0x23). Section 9.20.15 permits it in a SUBSCRIBE or a REQUEST_UPDATE for a subscription only: a fill fetch stream is something a subscription opens, and a FETCH already is one. Section 9.20.1 requires the receiver to close the session with a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION
vectors.error_detail: FILL_PARAMETERS may appear only in SUBSCRIBE or REQUEST_UPDATE for a subscription

vectors.description: FETCH with INCLUDE_PROPERTIES (0x35) carrying the value 255. Only 0 and 1 are allowed; anything else MUST close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (Section 9.20.21)
truncated FETCH — missing track_namespace
vectors.error_detail: unexpected end of input while reading track_namespace
